chapter: New Orleans ballrooms and Tony Almerico
title: Ballrooms and supper clubs in New Orleans
summary: They agree New Orleans never had a big Roseland-type ballroom, discussing the Fern, hotel ballrooms, the Blue Room and the Jung roof.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Well and they have, they had a good reason at one time. I think they've been tearing the Greystone Ballroom down if it's not going I think recently. I don't know. And that was a place that I used to hear people talk about a lot and still do. And of course I never remember there being a big ballroom here in this city like that.

I don't remember either, but then that would, see that would be like slightly before my time. Yeah. When ballrooms were popular. Yeah. I can remember Eddie Miller talking about the Fern Dance Hall. Yeah. And a couple more places if the names don't come to mind right now. And I imagine that maybe they were probably small scale ballrooms. Because it doesn't seem like New Orleans was the kind of town that would have a Roseland or something. No, no. Which is a monstrous thing.

You could dance with broken dishes at the Fern. Broken dishes mean Fawcett's girlfriend. That was not the Greystone Ball. But I absolutely do not ever remember going to a big ballroom except in a hotel. Yeah, all the hotels had ballrooms, but I don't think they were on a steady basis.
It would be like for dances. The Blue Room was going. Yeah, but that's not a ballroom. No. It was a supper club.
No. The Jung had a big room. The Jung had the cotillion. That also was a supper club. Well they had a roof at one time and the Los Radekos had a band there, but I don't recall.
I went to dances at high school proms and things on the roof of the Jung.
